page: Google Cloud Platform c4n-highcpu-48 is a compute-focused virtual machine instance powered by a dedicated 48-vCPU Intel Xeon 8581C processor with 24 physical cores operating at a base frequency of 2.3 GHz. The instance provides 96 GB of system memory, establishing a 2 GB per vCPU ratio tailored for CPU-bound computing rather than memory-heavy footprints. The CPU architecture includes a generous 260 MB shared L3 cache alongside advanced hardware vector extensions, notably AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX), enabling acceleration for low-precision matrix arithmetic and vector calculations. The configuration does not include local disk storage or onboard graphics processors, depending entirely on networked block storage for persistent data requirements.

Benchmark evaluations position this instance favorably in dense processing and multi-threaded throughput. It achieved a multi-core Geekbench score of 17,853 and a PassMark CPU score of 60,557.12, reflecting strong overall integer and floating-point capacity. Extended instruction execution and cryptographic operations perform exceptionally well, supported by dedicated hardware primitives for AES and SHA algorithms. The platform delivers top-tier results in text processing and image handling tests, alongside a Clang compilation score of 42,093. Benefiting from AMX matrix extensions, small-model language model inference achieved 3,649.93 prompt tokens per second and 386.47 generation tokens per second, which places it in the upper bracket of general CPU inference speeds.

Hardware tradeoffs for the c4n-highcpu-48 center on storage architecture and memory density. Memory bandwidth yields average figures (144.09 GB/s large block uncached read), and the lean 2:1 RAM-to-vCPU ratio limits suitability for massive in-memory databases or large analytical memory models. Furthermore, the absence of local ephemeral NVMe arrays mandates network I/O consideration for disk-intensive workflows. In contrast, the resource distribution maximizes compute-per-dollar efficiency when executing workloads that scale horizontally across processor threads without demanding proportional memory footprints. The instance functions best in roles such as CI/CD software compilation pipelines, media transcoding, cryptographic operations, high-concurrency static web serving, and lightweight AI/ML inference.
description: Google Cloud Platform c4n-highcpu-48 is a compute-aligned virtual machine engineered for high-throughput, multi-threaded workloads. Equipped with 48 dedicated vCPUs (24 physical cores) on an Intel Xeon 8581C processor running at 2.3 GHz and paired with 96 GB of system RAM, it maintains a 2 GB per vCPU ratio. The architecture features a large 260 MB L3 cache, AVX-512 vector support, and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for integer and floating-point acceleration. Benchmark data demonstrates strong multi-core execution, highlighted by a Geekbench multi-core score of 17,853, top-tier image and text processing ratings, and resilient static web serving reaching 75.61 GB/s. With no bundled local storage or integrated GPUs, persistence requires external network storage. This resource balance provides high efficiency for software build systems, parallel compression pipelines, batch processing, and CPU-driven machine learning inference.
